title: Boss: the job that said it was fine
summary: A sync that hides its failures, a nightly job that locks itself out after one bad night, and an error record pasted into a ticket. Make failures visible, safe and explained.

steps.title: Ticket FIN-402
body: *"Finance says the payroll export has not reached the share since Tuesday, but the sync job's log says `sync
complete` every night. Also, the nightly job has refused to run since it failed once, and the night operator pasted
a deploy error into DEP-1187 that nobody has read."*
Three scripts that each fail quietly, or fail once and then forever. A senior fixes the code so the next failure is

steps.title: sync complete (it was not)
prompt: - one file that cannot be copied does **not** stop the others;
- each failure is reported with the **file name** (a `Write-Warning` or `Write-Error` line);
- it exits **`1`** if anything failed, and `0` otherwise.

checks.name: a failure is reported and exits 1
checks.cmd: rm -f ~/share/exports/*; out=$(pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/sync-exports.ps1 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "$out"; test $rc = 1 && echo "$out" | grep -q 'payroll.csv' && test "$(echo "$out" | tail -n1 | tr -d '\r')" = 'copied 4, failed 1'
checks.fail: With `payroll.csv` unreadable, the script must name it, end with `copied 4, failed 1` and exit 1.

checks.name: the other four files are copied
checks.fail: The four readable files must still reach `~/share/exports` when one fails.

checks.name: a clean run exits 0
checks.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d); out=$(pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/sync-exports.ps1 -Source /opt/dojo/state/goodexports -Target "$d" 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "$out"; test $rc = 0 && test "$(echo "$out" | tail -n1 | tr -d '\r')" = 'copied 4, failed 0'
checks.fail: When every file copies, the last line should be `copied 4, failed 0` and the exit code 0.

checks.name: errors are no longer silenced
checks.fail: Remove `$ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'`: it is what hid the failure.

hints: `$ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'` threw every error away. Replace it with `'Stop'`, so each failure can be caught.
Put the `Copy-Item` in a `try`/`catch` **inside** the loop, count successes, and collect failed names in the `catch`.
After the loop: `"copied $copied, failed $($failed.Count)"` and `if ($failed.Count) { exit 1 }`.
solution: # sync-exports.ps1: copies the nightly exports to the finance share.
explain: `SilentlyContinue` for a whole script is almost always a bug waiting for a bad night. The pattern you wrote, *stop on
every error, catch per item, report, exit non-zero at the end*, is the standard shape of a batch job: partial
success is still delivered, and monitoring still finds out.

steps.title: Another run is in progress (forever)
prompt: `pwsh -File ~/scripts/nightly.ps1` refuses to run: a lock from last night's **failed** run is still there. The real
bug is in the script: when `work.ps1` fails (its input `~/data/input.csv` has not arrived), the lock is never
1. Fix `~/scripts/nightly.ps1` so the lock is removed **whatever happens**, while a failed run still fails
2. Then remove the stale lock (no other run is going on: you checked).

checks.name: the stale lock is gone
checks.fail: Remove `~/run/nightly.lock` once the script is fixed.

checks.name: a failed run fails and leaves no lock
checks.cmd: rm -f ~/data/input.csv ~/run/nightly.lock; pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/nightly.ps1 >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; echo "exit $rc"; test $rc -ne 0 && test ! -e ~/run/nightly.lock
checks.fail: Without `input.csv`, the run must exit non-zero **and** remove its lock. Wrap the work in `try { } finally { }`.

checks.name: a good run works and leaves no lock
checks.cmd:
rm -f ~/run/nightly.lock; printf 'id
1
2
' > ~/data/input.csv; out=$(pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/nightly.ps1 2>&1); rc=$?; rm -f ~/data/input.csv; echo "$out"; test $rc = 0 && echo "$out" | grep -q 'processed 2 rows' && echo "$out" | grep -q done && test ! -e ~/run/nightly.lock
checks.fail: With an input file, the run should print `processed 2 rows` and `done`, exit 0, and remove its lock.

checks.name: a real concurrent run is still refused
checks.cmd: echo busy > ~/run/nightly.lock; pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ~/scripts/nightly.ps1 >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; test -e ~/run/nightly.lock; ok=$?; rm -f ~/run/nightly.lock; test $rc -ne 0 && test $ok = 0
checks.fail: When another run holds the lock, the script must refuse **and leave that lock alone** (it belongs to the other run). Create the lock before `try`, not inside it.

hints: `Remove-Item -LiteralPath $lock` is the second-to-last line: a failing `work.ps1` (with `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`) jumps straight past it.

`try { & "$PSScriptRoot/work.ps1"; 'done' } finally { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $lock -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }`. `finally` runs on success, on error and on Ctrl+C, and the error still propagates.
Keep the `Test-Path`/`throw` and the `New-Item` **before** `try`, so a refused run never deletes the other run's lock. Then `Remove-Item ~/run/nightly.lock`.
solution: # nightly.ps1: makes sure only one nightly run happens at a time.
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $lock) { throw "Another run is in progress (lock: $lock)" }
explain: A lock without `finally` turns one failure into a permanent outage. Production versions add a timestamp and the
process id to the lock and treat a lock older than the longest possible run as stale, so a power cut cannot lock
the job out either. On Windows, a named mutex (`[System.Threading.Mutex]::new($false, 'Global\NightlyJob')`) does the

steps.title: Read the error record in DEP-1187
prompt: The night operator pasted `$Error[0] | Format-List * -Force` into the ticket: `Get-Content ~/incident/error.txt`.
1. Write what the record tells you into `~/answers/incident.txt`, exactly three `key=value` lines:
`Exception=` the exception's full type name, `Function=` the function that failed, `Line=` its line number in the script.
2. Fix the cause so the deploy can log as a normal user: give the script a **`-LogPath`** parameter (default still
`/var/log/deploy.log` for production) and use it in `Write-DeployLog`. `pwsh -File ~/deploy/deploy.ps1 -LogPath ~/logs/deploy.log`

checks.name: incident.txt reads the record correctly
checks.fail: `~/answers/incident.txt` should hold `Exception=...`, `Function=...` and `Line=...`. The type is at the start of the `Exception` line; `ScriptStackTrace` names the function and line, innermost first.

checks.name: -LogPath works
checks.fail: `deploy.ps1 -LogPath <file>` should exit 0 and append a line with `deployed 4.2.0` to that file.

hints: `Exception : System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path ... is denied.` The inner `IOException: Permission denied` confirms it is file permissions, not a missing folder.
`ScriptStackTrace` lists the innermost frame first: `at Write-DeployLog, .../deploy.ps1: line 27`.
Add `[string] $LogPath = '/var/log/deploy.log'` to the `param()` line and replace `-Path /var/log/deploy.log` with `-Path $LogPath`.
explain: Reading an error record top to bottom answers the three questions of every incident: *what* (the exception type
and message), *where* (`ScriptStackTrace`, `InvocationInfo`), and *with what* (`TargetObject`, here the log path).
`Write-DeployLog` reads `$LogPath` from the script scope, which works; in a module you would pass it as a parameter.
